lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Experience is not ordered newest-first.
items.because: The Aug 2022–Jul 2024 role appears before the Oct 2024–May 2025 role, so a reader could overlook the later internship.

items.says: The dashboard description states ownership without identifying a change you made.
items.because: The engineering work behind the responsibility is unclear, making it hard to distinguish from routine maintenance.

items.says: The on-call description adds a responsibility without showing what you did or what changed.
“Automated regression checks” does not identify the model-release regression being checked.
The line opens with a general maintenance duty instead of the change and its result.
The list of separate activities makes it unclear which work removed the nightly backlogs.
items.because: A reader may attribute the improvement to the combined list rather than the event-queue migration.

items.says: The backlog result is buried after the other activities.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss that it was the consequence of the migration.

items.says: The Eastern Robotics entry does not open with its strongest contribution.
“ML-extracted features” does not explain how the features informed triage.
Dynamic batching cannot explain a 40% latency reduction for single-request edge inference.
items.because: Batching combines concurrent requests; an isolated request has nothing to batch with.

items.says: The method-heavy opening buries the 5% latency result.
items.because: A scanning reader must get through the method details before reaching the outcome.

items.says: The 5% end-to-end latency result does not say what workflow was timed.
A single scored rollout per prompt cannot provide the group-relative reward comparison used by standard GRPO.
items.because: GRPO needs multiple scored rollouts per prompt, and the claim conflicts with the preceding bullet’s grouped rollouts.

items.says: “Stabilised” does not identify the instability resolved or an observable improvement.
The adoption claim does not identify the practice introduced or how you spread it.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what you built or changed across the platform.

items.says: The delivery and downstream benefits are too vague to show what changed.
items.because: Neither benefit identifies a workflow or prior state against which to judge the improvement.

items.says: The stated 50% reduction is mathematically wrong: 900 ms to 600 ms is about a 33% reduction.
items.because: The 300 ms decrease must be measured against the original 900 ms.

items.says: The stated 12% increase is wrong: 71% to 83% is an increase of 12 percentage points.
items.because: The relative increase from 71% would be about 16.9%.

items.says: The benchmark reference does not identify the tasks behind the completion rate.
The Agent Runtime Suite entry does not open with its strongest measured outcome.
The correlation does not identify the reference ordering used for comparison.
items.because: A reader needs to know what the evaluator’s scores were ranked against to interpret the 0.89 result.

items.says: The wording makes the trials sound like the actor removing material.
The defect categories do not show what any defect caused.
“Layered instrumentation” does not identify the signal that located the defects.
The upstream-fix wording obscures who made the fixes.
